newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends sharply down on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends sharply down on fund selling.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended sharply lower Thursday in response to spillover weakness from other CBOT pits and liquidation in September, pit traders said.
"The market opened on fund selling," said a pit trader. "There was long liquidation in September, in line with the corn and beans."
Some of the session's selling was sparked by perceptions that the U.S. rice crop is improving under favorable weather conditions, traders said.
USDA weekly export sales of 21,000 tonnes were regarded as neutral to futures by traders.
"Exports were okay," said one pit trader. "They didn't make us go down any."
Position holders in July were still noted liquidating positions and rolling into September and November, one pit trader said.
Volume was estimated at 2,000 contracts, which was above Wednesday's actual volume of 935 contracts.
Rice closed seven to 16-1/2 cents per cwt lower, with July down seven at $11.30 per cwt.
